title: How I built an interactive 38-scene voiced point-and-click browser game using AI illustration + Edge-TTS + React (Workflow breakdown and lessons learned)
author: Maximum-Policy-8340
selftext:
Hi everyone! 🚀



As a solo developer, building a point-and-click adventure game with dozens of fully voiced characters and multi-room illustrated environments was historically out of reach without a budget for an art and voice studio.



Over the past month, I built and shipped Aetheria Academy Journey — a 38-scene 2D point-and-click fantasy browser game. I wanted to share my complete pipeline, how I used AI as a force multiplier, and the real software engineering challenges required to glue it all together.



Live Game (Playable free in browser on desktop/mobile):

👉 [https://aetheria.inventkid.com/](https://aetheria.inventkid.com/)





THE AI PIPELINE:



1. Visual Asset Generation (2D Ghibli Aesthetic):

\- Generated 38 widescreen (16:9) scene backgrounds covering travel, castle interiors, four elemental house common rooms, dormitories, and secret gauntlet chambers.

\- Prompt consistency challenge: Getting a uniform art style across different room types required establishing a strict prompt anchor (2D anime Ghibli-style illustration, eye-level perspective, warm ambient lighting, no text/logos).

\- Landmark anchoring: For scenes that shared visual continuity (like common rooms and their connected dormitories), I kept color palettes and architectural motifs consistent across prompts (e.g. Pyralis: crimson and stone; Hydrus: lake columns and emerald; Zephyrus: blue and high arched cloud windows; Solis: warm wood, yellow patchwork, and plants).



2. Dual Audio Architecture (Neural Speech + Sound Synthesis):

\- Voice Acting: Extracted all in-game dialogue trees and narration pages into structured JSON, then ran automated Python scripts using Microsoft Edge-TTS neural models (e.g. ChristopherNeural for the enthusiastic young protagonist, GuyNeural/EmmaNeural for professors and portrait NPCs).

\- Sound FX: Instead of loading hundreds of static sound files, I built a custom Web Audio API oscillator synthesis engine in TypeScript to generate real-time audio effects directly in the browser (gate creaks, magic sparkles, owl hoots, gear grinding).





THE TRADITIONAL CODE & ARCHITECTURE BEHIND IT:



AI generated raw visual and audio assets, but turning them into an interactive game required custom React and TypeScript architecture:



1. Responsive Hotspot Coordinate Engine:

Mapped percentage-based coordinate bounding boxes across all 38 scenes so that portals, interactive inspect items, and dialogue triggers stay pixel-perfect on both mobile screens and 4K desktop viewports.



2. Global Spellcasting State Machine:

Built an interactive wand system. Players can pull up their wand from the toolbar, select spells (Lux, Ignis, Levitate, Reveal), and cast them on specific interactive hotspots in the world to trigger dynamic particle spawns, audio synthesis, and puzzle state changes.



3. Visual Novel Multi-Node Dialogue System:

Implemented branching dialogue trees with state persistence (e.g. the Fat Lady corridor guardian verifying passwords, headmaster dialogues, and NPC reactions).



4. Zero-Friction Browser Delivery:

Packaged everything into a lightweight single-page application with Vite and automated GitHub Actions CI/CD deploying directly to an AlmaLinux NVMe VPS via rsync.





LESSONS LEARNED FOR AI GAME DEVS:

\- Raw AI images alone are not a game. The hardest part is alignment — making sure interactive hitboxes feel natural against generated perspective lines.

\- Neural TTS + Web Audio synthesis is a game-changer for solo devs who want fully voiced narrative worlds with zero streaming latency.



Happy to answer any questions about the pipeline, prompts, coordinate mapping, or deployment!

comments.author: goddamnclever
comments.body:
the web audio oscillator part is what im most curious about. did you go that way for loading times or because you couldnt get decent generated sfx? and does it actually sound okay, i always assumed synthesized effects would end up sounding like an old nokia ringtone

also the hotspot alignment across 38 scenes, how long did that take? you said its the hardest part which is interesting, because thats the one piece AI didnt do for you

replies.author: Maximum-Policy-8340
replies.body:
On Web Audio: It was for both zero latency and instant response. Because it synthesizes audio in real time on the client, there are zero asset load delays. To avoid that 8-bit Nokia sound, I layered multiple oscillators with dynamic frequency ramps, exponential gain envelopes, white-noise buffer sources, and biquad filters (bandpass/lowpass). When shaped properly with reverb and harmonics, sounds like magical whooshes, sparkling spells, and creaking oak gates sound surprisingly organic and atmospheric.

On Hotspot Alignment: It took a couple of days overall. Because AI-generated scenes don't follow rigid 3D grid lines, perspective angles shift between rooms. I built a percentage-based coordinate system (x, y, width, height as percentages of the viewport) and used quick debug overlay scripts to test bounding boxes directly over the images. The trickiest part was ensuring hitboxes felt natural on both narrow mobile screens and ultrawide desktops without overlapping adjacent interactive objects.

comments.author: novokvest
comments.body: The AI-generated visuals here look incredibly clean and cohesive! Managing style consistency across a full adventure game environment is a huge challenge, and you did a fantastic job establishing a distinct mood for the universe. Really great proof of how generative assets can help a developer bring a large-scale world to life. I'm really excited to see more point-and-clicks made with AI!

replies.author: Maximum-Policy-8340
replies.body: Thanks, yes maintaining the vibe was very difficult but the output made it truly worth it!

replies.author: novokvest
replies.body: How long were you developing it? Are you planning on making a pac with classic third person protagonist walking the rooms?

replies.author: Maximum-Policy-8340
replies.body:
Took me 2 weeks of daily 3-4 hours development.

My very first idea was very similar, I thought of making an affiliate website in which we can explore the rooms from all sides, go to various rooms and explore a themed store.

I was always very fond of point and click based games, I am working on some other project currently but once I am done, will surely make a third person pac game (Always loved those indie puzzle based pac, mostly will fuse those concepts)
